title: Age weights change a fatality average
hook: Two stated cases: explore the population age composition of a descriptive risk.

knows: Reading the stated arithmetic assumptions and a small numerical chart
doesNotKnow: How the population age composition of a descriptive risk affects the stated comparison

misconception: The headline alone determines Gap, regardless of the stated inputs.
objective: Compare the population age composition of a descriptive risk in two explicit finite cases; separate model arithmetic from an empirical population claim.
keyState: Both question and changed cases computed; both parameter/result witnesses retained.

claims.text: Two toy strata have B rates 0.2,0.01; A is better by 0.01 in both. Stratum-1 shares are 0.2 in A, 0.8 in B. What is aggregate A minus B?

claims.text: Each stratum has the same stipulated advantage, but different weights can reverse the aggregate comparison. Equalizing weights removes this composition channel. This comparison isolates the population age composition of a descriptive risk.
